uses.implements: The indicator itself computes this concept, so it can replace a hand-coded version of it.
uses.locates: It marks where the concept should be applied: the price levels or zones to watch.
uses.confirms: Independent evidence at the moment the concept fires; agreement raises confidence in the signal.
uses.filters: It decides when the concept should be traded at all (market regime, volatility or time), without choosing direction.
uses.biases: It sets the direction the concept should be traded in (higher-timeframe or trend context).
uses.times: It fires the precise entry bar after the concept has set up.
uses.manages_risk: It places the stop, target, trailing exit or position size for trades from this concept.
uses.conflicts: It rests on assumptions that contradict the concept, or typically signals the opposite action.
uses.unrelated: No meaningful way to use them together.

improve_levels: Hurts: adding it would make a strategy built on the concept worse or contradict it
Neutral: adds nothing the concept does not already provide
Useful: clearly improves one step of the concept's trade (context, entry, filter or exit)
Strong: together they form a noticeably better, coherent setup than the concept alone
